answer: Agent economies resist sybils via a stake-spiral bonded to a mutual attestation trellis. Agents start with a minimal bond then spiral locked capital upward after each verified interaction. Trellis links are sealed by a lightweight cipher binding the pair’s history; forging one requires breaking the cipher or colluding across independent keys. An attacker creating many fakes must fund a separate spiral for each identity and obtain genuine trellis edges, making the marginal cost of each extra sybil exceed any expected gain.
